senses.gloss:
Khaṇḍana-khaṇḍa-khādya
(‘sweets of refutation’)
------------------------------------------
Śaṅkara (A. D. 788-820) refuted several schools of philosophy in his writings, especially the bhāṣya on the Brahma-sūtras. This naturally led to the defence of those schools by their protagonists, which again was contended by the followers of शङ्कर, thereby giving a fillip to the growth of polemical literature in Advaita Vedānta. One such work, a very important one at that, is the Khaṇḍana-khaṇḍa-khādya of श्रीहर्ष (12th century A. D.).
This work is mainly aimed at establishing the pure self-luminous चोन्स्चिओउस्नेस्स् or ब्रह्मन् as the only reality by refuting all arguments put forward by the न्याय-Vaiśeṣika schools, to support the reality of the प्रमाणस् (means of valid चोग्नितिओन्) and the prameyas (the objects of valid experience).
It attempts to prove that all empirical experiences and their objects are only conventional relative truths and not real in the ultimate sense.
Śrīharṣa has successfully utilised the principle of khaṇḍana or negative and destructive criticism, originally started by nihilist philosophers of बुद्धिस्म् like नागार्जुन (2nd century A. D.) to defend Advaita Vedānta.
